title: Certified Medical Translation vs. AI Translation
summary: Learn when healthcare teams need certified medical translation, when AI translation fits, and how to check accuracy, privacy, cost, and recipient rules.
body_markdown:
###


No. A 40-hour medical interpreter training certificate confirms course completion toward spoken interpretation eligibility, such as CCHI or NBCMI credentialing, and has no bearing on written translation certification. Document certification requires a signed attestation of accuracy and completeness from someone competent to translate, which is a separate qualification entirely.


###


No. USCIS requires a full English translation certified as complete and accurate by a competent translator. Opalite Health's AI output can serve as a draft for a qualified signer to review and attest to, but the software output alone cannot supply the required human attestation. Confirm the translator accepts AI-assisted drafts before assigning the work.


###


Certified medical translation is an attestation method: a signer declares the document accurate and complete. AI translation is a production method: software generates the translated text. The two are not competing services; a document can be produced by AI and then certified by a qualified human signer, as long as the recipient permits AI-assisted drafts.


###


Match every medication name, dose, unit, and frequency in the translated document against the source before distribution. Preserve negative statements such as "no known allergies" exactly, and verify allergy and dosing language using approved terminology resources. Validated automated checks can satisfy this requirement for low-risk reusable templates; high-risk or patient-specific content warrants targeted qualified review.


###


Route by intended use, not document title. Check whether the recipient, such as a court, insurer, or agency, requires a signed certification. If no certification is required and your policy permits AI-only translation, Opalite's output with validated accuracy checks can be released directly. If the form is headed to an official submission, send the Opalite draft to a qualified signer for complete review and signed certification before distributing it.
